newsitem.title: USA: Groups press for alternatives to Illinois tollways.
newsitem.headline: Groups press for alternatives to Illinois tollways.

text.p: A coalition of civic and public-interest groups Monday called on Illinois officials to consider alternatives to a proposed bond-financed extension of the tollway system in the northeastern part of the state.

"This region is at a crossroads, and state officials should seize this opportunity to step back and reexamine how we can most wisely invest in transportation infrastructure to meet our needs," said Howard Lerner, executive director of Chicago-based Environmental Law & Policy Center, in a news release.

He added that a recent U.S. District Court decision that stalled plans for a $700 million, 12.5-mile extension of I-355 represented "a chance for better regional transportation planning, rather than business as usual."

U.S. District Court Judge Suzanne Conlon ruled last month that Illinois failed to evaluate alternatives to the toll road or the effect the tollway extension would have on air quality. She directed state transportation officials to produce studies justifying their conclusions for the extension or explain why the studies were not possible.
The lawsuit had been brought by the environmental law center and other groups that claimed the environmental impact statement for the project was flawed.
Dave Loveday, a spokesman for the Illinois State Toll Highway Authority, said alternatives were examined by Illinois Department of Transportation.

He added that no decision was made on how to proceed in court with the lawsuit. One tollway official has said the authority could present the court more evidence to back up conclusions for the toll road extension or appeal Conlon's ruling.

In the news release, the groups said the federal court ruling cited assumptions in state transportation studies that justified the need for the tollway "according to a set of growth projections that might only come to pass if the tollway itself were built."
